title: Where is the altitude when the angle at the base is obtuse?
description: The base is extended beyond the obtuse corner and the set square is slid along the extended line until it touches the top corner. The perpendicular is then drawn, and a paper fold checks it. Keeko's doubt is that the altitude must stay inside the triangle.
teaching_notes: One idea: when a base angle is obtuse the altitude meets the extended base, so it lies outside the triangle. Watch for students who bend the altitude to keep it inside.

source: What would the altitude from A to BC be in this triangle? We extend BC and then drop the perpendicular from A to this line. Altitudes Using Paper Folding: Cut out a paper triangle. Fix one of the sides as the base. Fold it in such a way that the resulting crease is an altitude from the top vertex to the base. Justify why the crease formed should be perpendicular to the base.
video_script.why: The child can draw the altitude with a set square when it falls inside a triangle and now meets a triangle with an obtuse angle at the base.
video_script.substitution: A triangle ABC with an obtuse angle at B, the base BC extended beyond B, a ruler and a set square.
video_script.anchor: triangle ABC with an obtuse angle at B and its base BC
video_script.wrong_answer: the altitude must stay inside the triangle
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko bends the altitude to keep it inside the triangle, but then it meets the base at a slant and is not a perpendicular.
video_script.payoff_line: The altitude from eigh lies outside the triangle

final_answer.value: The altitude from A meets the extended base outside the triangle; the paper crease is perpendicular because its two equal angles add up to 180°
final_answer.spoken: the altitude from eigh meets the extended base outside the triangle

maths_rules: the angle at B is obtuse, so the perpendicular from A cannot meet the side BC itself
extend BC beyond B; slide the set square along the extended line until its upright edge touches A
the line drawn along the upright edge from A meets the extended line at the foot D, and D lies on the extension of BC beyond B
paper fold check: the base falls on itself with the crease through A; the two angles at the crease are equal and add up to 180°, so each is 180° ÷ 2 = 90°
video_script.design: The triangle with the obtuse corner at B stays on the board. The base is extended with a dotted line beyond B, the set square slides along it, and the paper fold is drawn as a side picture.
